Released 2026-11-14 · [downloads and checksums on GitHub](https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.12) · [Download page](/download/)
The twelfth beta of BackDown 1.0: the rest of the write-ahead log fix. If you're on beta.8 or earlier, this is the one to take.

beta.9 taught BackDown to reclaim the index's write-ahead log as it goes, which stops it growing while a long scan runs beside readers. This beta closes the other ways it could still grow. When a scan found that a great many files had gone — a drive emptied, a big folder moved away — it closed them all in one statement inside one transaction, and on a large index that one transaction could write more log than the index itself holds (47 GB, on 8 November). Forgetting a machine's cached files, or one of its drives, did the same over millions of rows. Both now go 20,000 rows at a time, the log reclaimed between batches. Syncing another machine's index is hours of pages, and nothing reclaimed the log between them: a status count or a report that outlasted a page held the log's growth for as long as it ran, and the file then kept that size for the rest of the sync (1 GB on a 17-million-file drive). Each page's commit reclaims it now, and so does the end of every background job. Reclaiming also no longer waits out the writer's 30-second patience behind a slow reader, and opening the index writes nothing when nothing has changed.

## Install

| Platform | Installer | Command line |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.12_amd64.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu) or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.12-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (static) |
| Linux ARM64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.12_arm64.deb` or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.12-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (static) |
| macOS (Apple silicon + Intel) | `BackDown-1.0.0-beta.12.dmg` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.12-macos-universal.tar.gz` |

Windows builds are paused for this beta while the port is finished; follow it at [https://github.com/BuenGenio/BackDown/issues/94](https://github.com/BuenGenio/BackDown/issues/94).

**This release is signed.** `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` is an Ed25519 signature of `SHA256SUMS.txt` by BackDown's release key, and `backdown update` checks it before installing anything. To check by hand, see [Air-gapped computers](https://backdown.io/docs/guides/air-gapped/).

The installers and apps themselves still aren't signed by Apple. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time (for the command-line binary: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown`).

## What's fixed since beta.9

- A scan that finds many files gone closes them 20,000 at a time, each batch committed and the write-ahead log reclaimed, instead of one statement over the whole drive: closing 200,000 files now leaves an 8 KB log where it left 44 MB, and the growth no longer scales with the index.
- Forgetting a machine's cached files (`backdown remote remove`, or a drive of it that was re-indexed from scratch) goes the same way: millions of rows, a batch at a time.
- Syncing another machine reclaims the log after every page of files it fetches, and every background job reclaims it when it finishes: a reader that outlasts a page no longer sets the log's size for the rest of the sync (60,000 files in 12 pages: 7 MB before, under 2 MB now).
- Reclaiming the log waits a quarter of a second for readers, not the writer's 30 seconds: a slow reader no longer stalls a scan at every batch, nor every command as it opens the index.
- Opening the index writes nothing when the schema is already current, so commands that only read never take the writer's lock.

## Known limitations

- Reverse-geocoding is to the nearest populated place of 1,000+ people; a photo far from any town takes the nearest one, with lower confidence. The named-place and airport matches are within a set distance.
- The name index takes some room: on 8.5 million distinct names, about 1.2 GB.
- Searching another machine at its fastest needs beta.7 or later there too.
- The installers aren't signed or notarised by Apple.
- Windows builds are paused this beta while the port is finished (#94); Linux and macOS are unaffected.
- Pro, Team and Forensic features are free during the beta; pricing may change before 1.0.

Documentation: https://backdown.io/docs/. Provided as-is, without warranty, for evaluation.
